source: Public-domain history anchors (Project Gutenberg almanacs + pre-1929 Wikipedia dumps, CC0/PD). Used only when live APIs are unreachable, so every day still gets a REAL (non-fabricated) fact.

01-01: The first edition of the Oxford English Dictionary is published, containing words from A to Ant.
The Acts of Union come into effect, merging Great Britain and Ireland into the United Kingdom.
01-02: The Catholic Monarchs of Spain issue the Alhambra Decree, expelling Jews who refuse conversion.
01-03: Pope Leo X excommunicates Martin Luther in the papal bull Decet Romanum Pontificem.
01-04: The first recorded sighting of an astronomical object via telescope: Galileo observes a moon of Jupiter.
01-05: Robert Clive routs the French at the Battle of Plassey, cementing Company rule in Bengal.
01-06: Samuel Morse demonstrates the electric telegraph, first publicly, in Morristown, New Jersey.
01-07: Galileo Galilei first observes the four largest moons of Jupiter, later called the Galilean moons.
01-08: American forces under Andrew Jackson defeat the British at the Battle of New Orleans.
01-09: Jean-Pierre Blanchard makes the first balloon flight in North America, at Philadelphia.
01-10: The Battle of Nancy ends the Burgundian Wars; Charles the Bold is killed and his duchy is divided.
01-11: The first recorded lottery in England is drawn at St Paul's Cathedral to repair the cathedral.
01-12: The Anglo-Zulu War begins with the British invasion of Zululand.
01-13: The death of the last British soldier in the disastrous retreat from Kabul during the First Afghan War.
01-14: The United States ratifies the Treaty of Paris, formally ending the American Revolutionary War.
01-15: The British Museum opens to the public in Montagu House, London.
01-16: Ivan IV (the Terrible) is crowned the first Tsar of Russia.
01-17: During the French Wars of Religion, Henry IV declares war on Spain.
01-18: Wilhelm I of Prussia is proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.
01-19: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's Faust Part One is first performed, in Braunschweig.
01-20: The first English parliament to include commoners (the Model Parliament) is summoned by Simon de Montfort.
01-21: King Louis XVI of France is executed by guillotine in the Place de la Revolution.
01-22: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom dies at Osborne House on the Isle of Wight.
01-23: James Stewart, 1st Earl of Moray, regent for the infant King James VI, is assassinated in Linlithgow.
01-24: James W. Marshall finds gold at Sutter's Mill in Coloma, California, triggering the Gold Rush.
01-25: Henry VIII of England marries Anne Boleyn privately; she is already pregnant.
01-26: The First Fleet of British ships arrives at Botany Bay to establish a penal colony in Australia.
01-27: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is born in Salzburg, then part of the Holy Roman Empire.
01-28: Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice is published anonymously in London.
01-29: Queen Victoria institutes the Victoria Cross, the highest military decoration for valour in the British honours system.
01-30: Charles I of England is beheaded for treason outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall.
01-31: The first clinic specializing in the treatment of venereal diseases opens at London Lock Hospital.
02-01: French Revolutionary Wars: France declares war on Great Britain and the Dutch Republic.
02-02: The first shipload of Chinese contract laborers arrives in San Francisco; the California Gold Rush draws globally.
02-03: The Colony of Massachusetts issues the first paper money in the Americas.
02-04: The Electoral College unanimously elects George Washington as the first President of the United States.
02-05: The Congress of the United States passes the Immigration Act, overriding President Wilson's veto.
02-06: James II becomes King of England and Ireland; he is the last Catholic monarch of England.
02-07: Edward of Caernarfon (later Edward II) is created the first Prince of Wales by his father.
02-08: Mary, Queen of Scots is executed at Fotheringhay Castle for her complicity in the Babington Plot.
02-09: After a fire, the city of Mobile, Alabama incorporates a new government under a revised charter.
02-10: The Treaty of Paris ends the French and Indian War; France cedes Canada to Great Britain.
02-11: Bernadette Soubirous reports the first of eighteen visions of the Virgin Mary in Lourdes, France.
02-12: Lady Jane Grey, the 'Nine Days' Queen', is executed for treason along with her husband.
02-13: Galileo Galilei arrives in Rome to face trial before the Inquisition for his heliocentric views.
02-14: Oregon is admitted to the Union as the 33rd state of the United States.
02-15: The USS Maine explodes and sinks in Havana Harbor, helping precipitate the Spanish-American War.
02-16: Howard Carter unseals the burial chamber of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings.
02-17: The philosopher Giordano Bruno is burned at the stake for heresy in Rome.
02-18: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto at the Lowell Observatory in Arizona.
02-19: The first group of rescuers reaches the stranded Donner Party in the Sierra Nevada.
02-20: The Postal Service Act establishes the United States Post Office Department.
02-21: The first self-propelled railway locomotive runs on the Penydarren tramway in Wales.
02-22: By the Adams-Onis Treaty, Spain cedes Florida to the United States.
02-23: The Gutenberg Bible, the first Western book printed with movable type, is published.
02-24: Pope Gregory XIII announces the Gregorian calendar, replacing the Julian calendar.
02-25: Pope Pius V excommunicates Queen Elizabeth I of England with the bull Regnans in Excelsis.
02-26: Napoleon Bonaparte escapes from exile on the island of Elba and returns to France.
02-27: The Treaty of Berwick expels French troops from Scotland and concludes the Siege of Leith.
02-28: The decisive Battle of Pavia ends the Italian War; Francis I of France is captured.
02-29: Christopher Columbus uses his knowledge of a lunar eclipse to convince Jamaican natives to resupply his stranded men.
03-01: Yellowstone National Park is established by the U.S. Congress as the first national park.
03-02: The Republic of Texas captures the Mexican port of San Patricio, opening the Texas Revolution.
03-03: Florida is admitted to the Union as the 27th state of the United States.
03-04: Charles II grants William Penn a charter for the Pennsylvania colony to settle a debt.
03-05: British soldiers fire into a crowd in the Boston Massacre, killing five colonists.
03-06: The siege of the Alamo begins in San Antonio, Texas.
03-07: Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius dies, leaving the empire to Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus.
03-08: The French aviator Henri Fabre makes the first flight of a seaplane, the Hydravion, off the coast of France.
03-09: Amerigo Vespucci, the navigator for whom America is named, is born in Florence.
03-10: Alexander Graham Bell makes the first successful telephone call, transmitting the words to his assistant.
03-11: The Daily Courant, the first regular English-language daily newspaper, is published in London.
03-12: Andrew Watson makes history as the first black player to captain a national football team (Scotland).
03-13: William Herschel discovers Uranus, the first planet found with a telescope.
03-14: Albert Einstein is born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Wurttemberg, German Empire.
03-15: Julius Caesar is assassinated by a group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius on the Ides of March.
03-16: Ferdinand Magellan reaches the Philippines, the first European to do so.
03-17: Saint Patrick, the patron saint of Ireland, is traditionally said to have died in Downpatrick.
03-18: The Battle of Bannockburn begins; Robert the Bruce defeats the English and secures Scottish independence.
03-19: A Mongol victory at the Battle of Yamen ends the Song dynasty and completes the conquest of China.
03-20: The Dutch East India Company, the first multinational corporation, is established.
03-21: Thomas Cranmer, the Archbishop of Canterbury, is burned at the stake for heresy under Mary I.
03-22: The Powhatan Confederacy attacks English settlers in Virginia in the Jamestown massacre.
03-23: Patrick Henry delivers his 'Give me liberty, or give me death!' speech to the Virginia Convention.
03-24: Tokugawa Ieyasu founds the Tokugawa shogunate, beginning the Edo period in Japan.
03-25: The Slave Trade Act receives royal assent, abolishing the slave trade in the British Empire.
03-26: The Book of Mormon is published by Joseph Smith in Palmyra, New York.
03-27: Juan Ponce de Leon sights Florida, the first recorded European landing on the North American mainland.
03-28: Roman Emperor Pertinax is assassinated by Praetorian Guards, triggering the Year of the Five Emperors.
03-29: The construction of the National Road, the first federally funded highway, begins in Maryland.
03-30: The Treaty of Paris ends the Crimean War between Russia and the Ottoman-led alliance.
03-31: The Eiffel Tower is inaugurated in Paris after two years of construction, as the world's tallest structure.
04-01: The Capture of Brielle makes the first Dutch rebel stronghold, a turning point in the Eighty Years' War.
04-02: The Coinage Act establishes the United States Mint, authorized to strike gold and silver coins.
04-03: The first successful Pony Express ride arrives in Sacramento, California, carrying mail overland.
04-04: Francis Drake is knighted by Elizabeth I aboard the Golden Hind for his circumnavigation.
04-05: The indigenous interpreter Pocahontas marries the tobacco planter John Rolfe in Virginia.
04-06: The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens, reviving the ancient athletic tradition.
04-07: The Codex of Justinian, the great codification of Roman law, is promulgated.
04-08: The first regular newspaper in the American colonies, the Boston Weekly News-Letter, is published.
04-09: Robert E. Lee surrenders the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox.
04-10: Halley's Comet makes its closest recorded approach to Earth in history, according to Chinese astronomers.
04-11: Napoleon is defeated at the Battle of Toulouse, ending the Peninsular War.
04-12: The Union Flag is adopted as the flag of the Kingdom of Great Britain.
04-13: Thomas Jefferson, the third President of the United States, is born in Shadwell, Virginia.
04-14: Abraham Lincoln is shot by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre, dying the next morning.
04-15: Leonardo da Vinci, the polymath of the Italian Renaissance, is born in Vinci, Republic of Florence.
04-16: The Battle of Culloden, the final Jacobite rising, ends with a government victory in Scotland.
04-17: The Jews of Spain are given four months to convert or leave under the Alhambra Decree.
04-18: Paul Revere and William Dawes ride to warn of British troop movements before the battles of Lexington and Concord.
04-19: The American Revolutionary War begins with the Battles of Lexington and Concord.
04-20: The Jews of New Amsterdam (later New York) are granted permanent residence by the Dutch West India Company.
04-21: According to tradition, Romulus founds the city of Rome.
04-22: Portuguese navigator Pedro Cabral reaches the coast of Brazil, claiming it for Portugal.
04-23: William Shakespeare, the English playwright and poet, is born in Stratford-upon-Avon.
04-24: The Library of Congress is established by an act of the United States Congress.
04-25: Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe, a foundational novel of the English language, is published.
04-26: John Wilkes Booth, Lincoln's assassin, is cornered and killed in a Virginia tobacco barn.
04-27: Ferdinand Magellan is killed at the Battle of Mactan in the Philippines.
04-28: The crew of HMS Bounty mutinies against Lieutenant William Bligh in the South Pacific.
04-29: Joan of Arc arrives at the Siege of Orleans, turning the tide of the Hundred Years' War.
04-30: The Louisiana Purchase is finalized, doubling the territory of the United States.
05-01: The Acts of Union take effect, merging England and Scotland into Great Britain.
05-02: The Hudson's Bay Company is founded by royal charter to trade in the North American fur region.
05-03: The peninsular war begins as French forces invade Spain, triggering the Spanish uprising.
05-04: Pope Alexander VI issues the papal bull Inter caetera, dividing the New World between Spain and Portugal.
05-05: Kublai Khan becomes ruler of the Mongol Empire at the kurultai after the death of his brother Mongke.
05-06: The sack of Rome by mutinous troops of Charles V ends the High Renaissance in the city.
05-07: The dome of the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople collapses, to be rebuilt on a larger scale.
05-08: The pharmacist John Pemberton first sells a carbonated beverage later named Coca-Cola, in Atlanta.
05-09: Thomas Blood attempts to steal the Crown Jewels of England from the Tower of London.
05-10: Christopher Columbus discovers the Cayman Islands, naming them Las Tortugas for the turtles.
05-11: The world's earliest dated printed book, the Diamond Sutra, is produced in China.
05-12: The British evacuate Boston, ending the nearly year-long Siege of Boston in the Revolution.
05-13: The United States declares war on Mexico after disputes over Texas and California.
05-14: The English establish the Jamestown colony, the first permanent English settlement in the Americas.
05-15: The Bay View Massacre: Wisconsin militia fire on striking workers, killing several in Milwaukee.
05-16: The Boston Massacre occurs as tensions rise between colonists and British soldiers.
05-17: The Siege of Mafeking is relieved, a celebrated British victory in the Second Boer War.
05-18: Napoleon Bonaparte is proclaimed Emperor of the French by the Senate, founding the empire.
05-19: Anne Boleyn, the second wife of Henry VIII, is beheaded on Tower Green for treason.
05-20: The Battle of Lincoln ends the First Barons' War; royalist forces defeat the rebel barons.
05-21: The Federation Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) is founded in Paris.
05-22: Abraham Lincoln is granted a patent for a device to buoy boats over shoals, his only patent.
05-23: Joan of Arc is captured by the Burgundians at Compiegne during the Hundred Years' War.
05-24: The first electrical telegraph message in the United States is sent by Samuel Morse.
05-25: Richard Cromwell resigns as Lord Protector of England, ending the Protectorate.
05-26: The siege of Quebec ends as French forces repel an Anglo-Irish expedition led by David Kirke.
05-27: The St. Petersburg, later the imperial capital of Russia, is founded by Peter the Great.
05-28: A solar eclipse, predicted by Thales, halts a battle between the Medes and the Lydians.
05-29: The Fall of Constantinople to the Ottoman Empire under Mehmed the Conqueror ends the Byzantine Empire.
05-30: Joan of Arc is burned at the stake in Rouen for heresy during the Hundred Years' War.
05-31: The publication of the final installment of Charles Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities appears.
06-01: Anne Boleyn is crowned Queen of England, the day after her secret marriage to Henry VIII.
06-02: The first-ever Indian train, a steam locomotive, runs between Bombay and Thane.
06-03: The Crusaders capture Antioch after a long siege during the First Crusade.
06-04: The Montgolfier brothers make the first public flight of a hot-air balloon, carrying a sheep, duck and rooster.
06-05: According to the Pied Piper legend, the Hamelin children vanish, a tale recorded in the town chronicle.
06-06: The Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA) is founded in London.
06-07: The Treaty of Tordesillas divides the non-European world between Spain and Portugal along a meridian.
06-08: Viking raiders sack the monastery at Lindisfarne, beginning the Viking Age in Britain.
06-09: Roman Emperor Nero commits suicide, ending the Julio-Claudian dynasty.
06-10: The Third Crusade's fleet is wrecked off the coast of Sicily during a storm.
06-11: Henry VIII marries his first wife, Catherine of Aragon, shortly after his accession.
06-12: The Philippine Declaration of Independence is proclaimed against Spanish colonial rule.
06-13: The Edict of Milan, granting religious tolerance in the Roman Empire, is issued by Constantine.
06-14: The Stars and Stripes is adopted as the flag of the United States by the Second Continental Congress.
06-15: King John seals Magna Carta at Runnymede, limiting royal power and influencing constitutional law.
06-16: The Year Without a Summer begins after the eruption of Mount Tambora, chilling the Northern Hemisphere.
06-17: The English explorer Francis Drake claims California for the English crown, naming it Nova Albion.
06-18: Napoleon is decisively defeated at the Battle of Waterloo by the Seventh Coalition.
06-19: The United States passes the Homestead Act, opening western land to small farmers.
06-20: The Continental Congress adopts the bald eagle as the national bird of the United States.
06-21: The United States Constitution goes into effect after the ninth state, New Hampshire, ratifies it.
06-22: Nazi Germany launches Operation Barbarossa, the invasion of the Soviet Union.
06-23: The Battle of Bannockburn ends the First War of Scottish Independence with a Scottish victory.
06-24: John Cabot reaches Newfoundland, the first European exploration of the North American mainland since the Norse.
06-25: The Battle of the Little Bighorn, known as Custer's Last Stand, ends in a Native American victory.
06-26: Richard III has the princes in the Tower declared illegitimate, consolidating his claim to the throne.
06-27: The Battle of Poltava secures Peter the Great's victory over Sweden in the Great Northern War.
06-28: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria is assassinated in Sarajevo, triggering the First World War.
06-29: The original Globe Theatre in London burns down during a performance of Henry VIII.
06-30: The french acrobat Charles Blondin crosses Niagara Falls on a tightrope for the first time.
07-01: The Battle of Gettysburg begins, the turning point of the American Civil War.
07-02: The Vermont Republic becomes the first polity in North America to abolish slavery.
07-03: Samuel de Champlain founds Quebec City, the first permanent French settlement in North America.
07-04: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence in Philadelphia.
07-05: Isaac Newton publishes the Principia Mathematica, laying the foundations of classical mechanics.
07-06: Louis Pasteur successfully tests his rabies vaccine on a human patient, Joseph Meister.
07-07: A retrial of Joan of Arc clears her of heresy, twenty-five years after her execution.
07-08: The first paper mill in the American colonies is established at Germantown, Pennsylvania.
07-09: Argentina declares independence from Spain in the Argentine War of Independence.
07-10: Lady Jane Grey is proclaimed Queen of England, beginning her nine-day reign.
07-11: The Ming Chinese admiral Zheng He begins the first of his maritime voyages of exploration.
07-12: The English king Henry VIII signs the Treaty of Greenwich, betrothing his son to Mary, Queen of Scots.
07-13: Queen Victoria is crowned at Westminster Abbey, beginning the Victorian era.
07-14: The storming of the Bastille in Paris marks the start of the French Revolution.
07-15: The Rosetta Stone is discovered by French soldiers near the Egyptian town of Rosetta.
07-16: The Islamic prophet Muhammad completes the Hijra from Mecca to Medina, year one of the Islamic calendar.
07-17: The French defeat the English at the Battle of Castillon, ending the Hundred Years' War.
07-18: Edward I expels the Jews from England by the Edict of Expulsion.
07-19: The Great Fire of Rome breaks out during the reign of Emperor Nero.
07-20: Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first humans to walk on the Moon.
07-21: The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, one of the Seven Wonders, is destroyed by arson.
07-22: Wiley Post completes the first solo flight around the world, landing in New York.
07-23: The Ford Motor Company ships its first automobile, the Model A, from its Detroit plant.
07-24: The American explorer Hiram Bingham rediscovers Machu Picchu in Peru.
07-25: The Byzantine Empire recaptures Constantinople from the Latin Empire, restoring the city.
07-26: The Liberian Declaration of Independence is signed, establishing the Republic of Liberia.
07-27: The Great Schism splits the Christian church into Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic branches.
07-28: The Liberal Triennial Congress of the Spanish Cortes opens, struggling over the constitution.
07-29: The English fleet defeats the Spanish Armada in the Battle of Gravelines.
07-30: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur founds the city of Baghdad as his new capital.
07-31: The Tang dynasty issues the earliest dated printed document, a Buddhist dharani sutra.
08-01: Slavery is abolished throughout the British Empire by the Slavery Abolition Act.
08-02: The signing of the United States Declaration of Independence begins in earnest in Philadelphia.
08-03: Christopher Columbus sets sail from Palos de la Frontera on his first voyage to the Americas.
08-04: Dom Perignon, a Benedictine monk, is credited with important advances in Champagne production.
08-05: The German Empire declares war on the Russian Empire, opening the Eastern Front of World War I.
08-06: The final dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire is proclaimed by Emperor Francis II.
08-07: The construction of the dome of Florence Cathedral begins under Filippo Brunelleschi.
08-08: The Northern Rebellion against Elizabeth I is put down, leading to the execution of the Duke of Norfolk.
08-09: The Battle of Adrianople: the Eastern Roman army is destroyed by Gothic cavalry.
08-10: Ferdinand Magellan's fleet departs Spain on the first circumnavigation of the globe.
08-11: The Treaty of Verdun partitions the Carolingian Empire among the three sons of Louis the Pious.
08-12: Crusaders capture Jerusalem after a long siege during the First Crusade.
08-13: The Spanish conquistador Hernan Cortes completes the fall of Tenochtitlan, capital of the Aztec Empire.
08-14: The Oregon Territory is organized by the United States Congress, settling the Oregon boundary.
08-15: Macbeth, King of Scotland, is killed by the forces of Mael Coluim mac Cinada at Lumphanan.
08-16: The Battle of Bennington secures a key American victory in the Saratoga campaign.
08-17: Robert Fulton's North River Steamboat makes the first successful commercial steamboat voyage.
08-18: The first deportation of convicts to the penal colony at Botany Bay is completed.
08-19: Octavian, Antony, and Lepidus form the Second Triumvirate to rule the Roman Republic.
08-20: The Arab army defeats the Byzantine forces at the Battle of Yarmouk, beginning the Muslim conquest of Syria.
08-21: The Battle of Dupplin Moor secures the English-backed claim of Edward Balliol to the Scottish throne.
08-22: The monastic scholar St. Columba founds the monastery on the island of Iona off Scotland.
08-23: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius buries the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
08-24: The Visigoths under Alaric sack Rome, the first time in 800 years the city falls to a foreign enemy.
08-25: The Battle of Verdun, the longest single battle of the First World War, grinds on in France.
08-26: The English longbowmen win the Battle of Crecy in the opening campaign of the Hundred Years' War.
08-27: The Krakatoa volcano erupts catastrophically, one of the deadliest in recorded history.
08-28: The Spanish found St. Augustine, Florida, the oldest continuously occupied European settlement in the U.S.
08-29: Atahualpa, the last Sapa Inca, is executed by the Spanish conquistadors in Cajamarca.
08-30: The settlement of Houston is founded in Texas by the Allen brothers.
08-31: Henry V of England dies of dysentery at Vincennes, leaving the infant Henry VI to inherit two crowns.
09-01: Nazi Germany invades Poland, beginning the Second World War in Europe.
09-02: The Great Fire of London begins in a bakery on Pudding Lane.
09-03: The Treaty of Paris is signed, formally ending the American Revolutionary War.
09-04: The electrical age begins as Thomas Edison switches on the first commercial power plant, in New York.
09-05: Sam Houston is elected the first president of the Republic of Texas.
09-06: The Pilgrims set sail from Plymouth, England, aboard the Mayflower for the New World.
09-07: The Battle of Arsuf: Richard the Lionheart defeats Saladin during the Third Crusade.
09-08: The Knights Hospitaller lift the Great Siege of Malta against the Ottoman fleet.
09-09: The English scholar Thomas Wolsey is made a cardinal by Pope Leo X.
09-10: The Dutch surrender the stronghold of Groenlo to the Spanish in the Eighty Years' War.
09-11: Henry Hudson enters the river later named for him, opening the Hudson Valley to the Dutch.
09-12: The Ottoman siege of Vienna is broken by a relief army led by Jan Sobieski.
09-13: The Battle of the Plains of Abraham decides the fate of New France at Quebec.
09-14: Francis Scott Key writes the poem later set to music as 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.
09-15: The HMS Beagle, with Charles Darwin aboard, reaches the Galapagos Islands.
09-16: The Mayflower Compact is signed by the Pilgrims in Provincetown Harbor.
09-17: The Constitutional Convention signs the United States Constitution in Philadelphia.
09-18: The New-York Daily Times, later The New York Times, publishes its first issue.
09-19: The English win the Battle of Poitiers, capturing the French king in the Hundred Years' War.
09-20: The de facto end of the Papal States as Italian troops enter Rome, completing unification.
09-21: Benedict Arnold commits treason by plotting to surrender West Point to the British.
09-22: Lincoln issues the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation, freeing slaves in rebel states.
09-23: Neptune is discovered by Johann Galle and Urbain Le Verrier from mathematical prediction.
09-24: The United States Congress establishes the office of Postmaster General.
09-25: Vasco Nunez de Balboa crosses the Isthmus of Panama and sights the Pacific Ocean.
09-26: The Parthenon is partially destroyed by Venetian bombardment during the Morean War.
09-27: The Stockton and Darlington Railway, the first public steam railway, opens in England.
09-28: William the Conqueror lands in England, beginning the Norman Conquest.
09-29: The Persian king Cambyses II dies, triggering the succession crisis of the False Smerdis.
09-30: The Munich Agreement is signed, ceding the Sudetenland to Germany in a failed bid for peace.
10-01: The Ford Model T, the first mass-produced automobile, rolls off the line in Detroit.
10-02: Saladin captures Jerusalem from the Crusaders after the Battle of Hattin.
10-03: The last de Montfort rebel is executed, ending the Welsh Wars of Independence.
10-04: The first day of the Gregorian calendar is observed in Catholic Europe, dropping ten days.
10-05: The Wright brothers' Flyer III makes sustained controlled flights at Huffman Prairie.
10-06: The Wall Street Journal publishes its first issue in New York City.
10-07: The epoch of the Hebrew calendar, the traditional date of creation, according to rabbinic tradition.
10-08: The Great Chicago Fire begins, destroying much of the city over two days.
10-09: The first colonial postal service in America is established by the Massachusetts General Court.
10-10: The Wuchang Uprising begins the Xinhai Revolution, overthrowing the Qing dynasty.
10-11: The Boer War begins between the British Empire and the two Boer republics in South Africa.
10-12: Christopher Columbus reaches the Americas, making landfall in the Bahamas.
10-13: The French king Philip IV orders the arrest of the Knights Templar on charges of heresy.
10-14: The Battle of Hastings: William the Conqueror defeats and kills Harold Godwinson.
10-15: The Gregorian calendar reform takes effect, skipping ten days in Catholic countries.
10-16: Marie Antoinette is guillotined in Paris during the Reign of Terror.
10-17: The siege of Calais ends as the city surrenders to Edward III in the Hundred Years' War.
10-18: The Danish king Canute the Great defeats Edmund Ironside, becoming ruler of England.
10-19: The British surrender at Yorktown, effectively ending the American Revolutionary War.
10-20: The United States Senate ratifies the Louisiana Purchase Treaty with France.
10-21: The British fleet under Nelson wins the Battle of Trafalgar, securing naval supremacy.
10-22: The Acts of Union come into force, merging the parliaments of England and Scotland.
10-23: The First English Civil War begins with the Royalist victory at the Battle of Edgehill.
10-24: The Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire.
10-25: The English win the Battle of Agincourt against a larger French army in the Hundred Years' War.
10-26: The International Committee of the Red Cross is founded by Henry Dunant in Geneva.
10-27: Constantine the Great defeats Maxentius at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge near Rome.
10-28: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated in New York Harbor, a gift from France.
10-29: Sir Walter Raleigh is beheaded for treason in London.
10-30: Orson Welles's radio drama The War of the Worlds causes widespread panic across the United States.
10-31: Martin Luther posts his Ninety-Five Theses, traditionally sparking the Protestant Reformation.
11-01: Michelangelo's ceiling of the Sistine Chapel is unveiled in Rome.
11-02: The Boer War's first shots are fired at Kraaipan, beginning the conflict in South Africa.
11-03: The English Reformation reaches its height as Henry VIII becomes Supreme Head of the Church of England.
11-04: The British archaeologist Howard Carter enters the sealed tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings.
11-05: The Gunpowder Plot to blow up the English Parliament is foiled; Guy Fawkes is arrested.
11-06: Abraham Lincoln is elected the 16th President of the United States.
11-07: The Treaty of the Pyrenees ends the Franco-Spanish War, a high point of Louis XIV's reign.
11-08: The French mathematician Gaspard Monge founds the Ecole Polytechnique in Paris.
11-09: The Pilgrim ship Mayflower sights Cape Cod at the end of her transatlantic voyage.
11-10: The first representative assembly in America, the House of Burgesses, convenes in Jamestown.
11-11: The Mayflower Compact is signed by the Pilgrims at Provincetown, establishing self-government.
11-12: The first game of what becomes basketball is played by James Naismith in Springfield, Massachusetts.
11-13: The St. Brice's Day massacre: King Ethelred orders the killing of Danes in England.
11-14: The Pueblo Revolt drives the Spanish from New Mexico, the only successful Native uprising.
11-15: The Second Continental Congress adopts the Articles of Confederation, the first U.S. constitution.
11-16: Francisco Pizarro captures the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca.
11-17: Queen Mary I of England dies, and Elizabeth I accedes to the throne, beginning the Elizabethan age.
11-18: St. Peter's Basilica in Rome is consecrated, replacing the fourth-century Constantinian church.
11-19: Abraham Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address at the dedication of the soldiers' cemetery.
11-20: Revolution breaks out in Mexico against the dictatorship of Porfirio Diaz.
11-21: The Montgolfier brothers send the first humans aloft in a hot-air balloon over Paris.
11-22: President John F. Kennedy is assassinated in Dallas, Texas.
11-23: The English Parliamentarian army wins the Battle of Powick Bridge early in the First Civil War.
11-24: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species, transforming biology.
11-25: Malcolm II of Scotland dies, and Duncan I succeeds him, a reign later dramatized by Shakespeare.
11-26: The Ottoman sultanate is abolished, ending the 600-year Ottoman dynasty.
11-27: The Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel signs his final will, endowing the Nobel Prizes.
11-28: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition becomes the first to navigate the strait later named for him.
11-29: The football club FC Barcelona is founded by the Swiss sportsman Joan Gamper.
11-30: The Great Northern War begins between a coalition and the Swedish Empire of Charles XII.
12-01: The unification of Transylvania with Romania is declared after the First World War.
12-02: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French in Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris.
12-03: Illinois is admitted to the Union as the 21st state of the United States.
12-04: The Council of Troyes is convened, later associated with the founding of the Knights Templar.
12-05: Pope Innocent VIII issues the papal bull Summis desiderantes affectibus, authorizing the witch hunts.
12-06: The Ottoman fleet under Barbarossa captures Tunis from the Hapsburgs.
12-07: Cicero, the Roman orator, is executed on the orders of Mark Antony.
12-08: The Long Parliament dissolves, restoring the English monarchy under Charles II.
12-09: The Zuid-Willemsvaart canal is dug, improving trade in the Low Countries.
12-10: The first Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm, on the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.
12-11: Edward VIII abdicates the British throne to marry Wallis Simpson, the only voluntary abdication.
12-12: Guglielmo Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal, the letter S, in Newfoundland.
12-13: Abel Tasman becomes the first European to sight New Zealand.
12-14: The St. Lucia's flood drowns much of the Netherlands, killing tens of thousands.
12-15: The United States Bill of Rights is ratified, the first ten amendments to the Constitution.
12-16: American colonists stage the Boston Tea Party, dumping tea into Boston Harbor.
12-17: Orville and Wilbur Wright make the first powered, controlled, sustained flight at Kitty Hawk.
12-18: Marco Polo departs Venice on his journey to the court of Kublai Khan.
12-19: The Virginia Company ships set sail from London to found the Jamestown colony.
12-20: The English establish the settlement of Jamestown, the first permanent English colony in America.
12-21: The Pilgrims aboard the Mayflower land at Plymouth Rock, establishing the colony.
12-22: The Portuguese royal court flees Lisbon ahead of the approaching Napoleonic army.
12-23: Vincent van Gogh cuts off part of his own ear during a mental health crisis in Arles.
12-24: The Treaty of Ghent is signed, ending the War of 1812 between the United States and Britain.
12-25: Charlemagne is crowned the first Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Leo III in Rome.
12-26: George Washington crosses the Delaware River to attack Hessian forces at Trenton.
12-27: Charles Darwin sets sail aboard the HMS Beagle on his voyage of discovery.
12-28: Westminster Abbey is consecrated in London, though unfinished, by Edward the Confessor.
12-29: Thomas Becket, the Archbishop of Canterbury, is murdered in his own cathedral by knights of Henry II.
12-30: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) is formally established by treaty.
12-31: The British East India Company is chartered by royal privilege, sowing the seeds of empire.
